assertions.description: HTMLAnchorElement.prototype has a windowFeatures IDL attribute. This is the explainer's own API-support detection for split tabs.
The windowFeatures IDL attribute on <a> reflects the windowfeatures content attribute (getter returns the attribute string).
assertions.test: (() => { const a = document.createElement('a'); a.setAttribute('windowfeatures', 'split,splitposition=right,splitsize=40'); return a.windowFeatures === 'split,splitposition=right,splitsize=40'; })()

assertions.description: Setting a.windowFeatures writes the windowfeatures content attribute.
assertions.test: (() => { const a = document.createElement('a'); a.windowFeatures = 'split'; return a.getAttribute('windowfeatures') === 'split'; })()

assertions.description: HTMLAreaElement.prototype has a windowFeatures IDL attribute (the declarative form applies to <area>).
HTMLFormElement.prototype has a windowFeatures IDL attribute (form submissions can request a split).

window.open(url, '_blank', 'split,splitposition=right,splitsize=40') with transient activation opens the content in a split tab next to the opener, keeps the opener relationship, and returns a WindowProxy.
assertions.test: Needs a user click, a browser with a split-view UI and WindowOpenSplitTab enabled. The result cannot be read back by design (no result API). Observe it in /v158/opening-links-in-a-split-tab/split-request-playground/.

assertions.description: When a split is not created (unsupported UI, narrow window, window already split), a 'popup=0,split' request opens an ordinary new tab, not a popup. With 'split,popup' the fallback is a popup instead.
assertions.test: Needs a user click and window.open(); the opened view's toolbar.visible distinguishes popup from tab. Observe it in /v158/opening-links-in-a-split-tab/fallback-lab/.
